The dynamic plant modeler and nursery natFX, which interfaces with an architectural plant model AMAPmod (Bionatics, CIRAD, Montpellier, France), iss used to simulate the forest stands. Tree descriptions are available for beech ( Fagus sylvatica L.) and poplar ( Populus nigra L. var. â italica â Muench), two in Western Europe wide-spread forest species with distinct structural differences. All leaves are assigned a species-specific reflectance and transmittance spectrum extracted from the LOPEX (Leaf Optical Properties Experiment) dataset. For the forest scene illumination a skymap developed by [10] is used. Average direct and indirect solar illumination is simulated in the raytracer at the average monthly solar positions at 12.30 pm, from April until September.
          
           To achieve a nearly 100% canopy cover the average tree spacing is set at 5m for beech, and 1m for poplar. The dataset comprises of a series of six forest scenes providing a gradual transition from a forest scene completely dominated by one species to a scene dominated by the other species (see figure below). In each
step, 20% of the Fagus trees are randomly replaced by a block of 3x3 Populus trees. The spatial resolution is fixed at 30m to simulate spaceborne hyperspectral sensors. As reference data, only the fraction maps are provided for the six hyperspectral images, showing the true areal coverage of the two tree species, which sum up to one. For the reference pure signature, the first (100% Beech) and the last image (100% Poplar) of the sequence can be used to provide the reference signatures of the two components. While in the virtual orchard one signature per component was used for the whole image, a pixel-specific endmember is needed for the virtual forest scenes due to the variability in tree properties throughout the forest. No background endmember is needed as there is no background present in the image due to the complete coverage of the trees. In addition, the influence of the background on the pure tree signatures is taken into account in the endmember definition (i.e. the same background is present in the 100% Beech and 100% Poplar image as in the mixed pixels).
